subject.name: NodeRoom note-shaped surfaces, baseline — color and elevation on NoteworthyInbox and NotebookDigestWorkbench
subject.surface: Color carriers in NoteworthyInbox (src/app/styles.css:220-261, 2547-2552) and NotebookDigestWorkbench (src/ui/workArtifacts/work-artifacts.css:1503-2050). NodeRoom's own accent is terracotta #D97757 (accent-ink #e59579); Mew's teal transfers as a rule, never as a hue.
subject.evidenceRef: source checkout, noderoom worktree at commit 9c99889f: work-artifacts.css:1666-1668 (data-type hue), 1634-1643 (block index chips), styles.css:220 (popover shadow), 232-235 (status pill tones)

appliesWhenSatisfied: text-dominant surfaces where inline metadata must be scannable: digest block meta rows carry kind/type/role/status labels inline; inbox items carry entity names, reasons, and source kinds
dark-first product where saturation fatigues quickly: NodeRoom ships a dark theme with terracotta as its single named accent (RoomShell ACCENTS map holds exactly one key)

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: data visualization surfaces needing categorical palettes (dataviz skill governs there)
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: Neither surface renders a chart. Kernel chart output in the digest is summarized as a text line (type, axes, point count), not plotted.

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: status-heavy dashboards where semantic red/amber/green carry meaning the accent cannot
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: These are entry lists, not status dashboards. Semantic state colors that do appear — danger on failed inbox items, green on accepted/ready digest states, warning on suggested pills — carry decision-relevant state on trust surfaces and are exempted per element rather than disqualifying the surface. The rule is applied here to non-semantic color only, and no fix may touch trust-surface state styling (rule-single-accent-inline may not override trust-surface neutrality).

anchors.0: two or more non-semantic hues loose in body text and the accent spent on per-entry decoration — color cannot function as a retrieval signal
anchors.1: one foreign non-semantic hue remains inline, or the accent decorates every entry uniformly
anchors.2: no foreign inline hue and no per-entry accent decoration, but no meaningful inline accent carrier exists either — color encodes nothing retrievable
anchors.3: the accent is carried by meaningful inline elements; chrome accent or elevation still sits past the measured bound (shadows over 8px blur or above 0.067 alpha, obs-mew-tokens/f5)
anchors.4: one accent hue carried only by meaningful inline elements, achromatic chrome, every shadow within the measured tokens (obs-mew-tokens/f1, f5)

criteria.question: Does any non-semantic hue outside the app accent appear on inline elements?

citations.note: Mew holds a single accent hue with a full ramp. The digest paints block-type labels periwinkle #b8c7ff (work-artifacts.css:1666-1668) — a second, unrelated hue with no token behind it, on the most repeated inline metadata element.

In Mew, inline hashtags and links are the only colored body-text elements, all in the accent. Here the colored inline element carries a hue that is not the accent, so color stops being a reliable signal for anything.

criteria.finding: One foreign non-semantic hue (#b8c7ff) rides every typed block's meta row. Green #55d49a on accepted/ready is semantic state and exempt.

criteria.question: Is the accent spent on uniform per-entry decoration rather than on meaning?

citations.note: Every digest block renders an accent-tinted, accent-inked index chip (work-artifacts.css:1634-1643) regardless of state or meaning. Accent on all 48 visible blocks equally is decoration: it distinguishes nothing.

criteria.finding: The block index chip spends the accent uniformly on every entry, which is the opposite of color-as-retrieval-signal: a terracotta element should mean something is there.

criteria.question: Does any meaningful inline element carry the accent, making color a retrieval signal?

citations.note: In the inbox, entity names — the retrievable token, this surface's analog of a hashtag — render as plain bold text (styles.css:255). The accent appears on buttons and the practice panel border instead. Nothing inline in body text carries the accent on either surface.

criteria.finding: No inline accent carrier exists. The accent lives on affordances (batch-research button, practice panel) while the one element a reader would scan for — the entity name — is achromatic.

criteria.question: Do shadows stay within the measured bound — at most 8px blur at 0.05-0.067 alpha?

citations.note: Mew's three shadow tokens all stay at or under 8px blur, alpha 0.05-0.067. The inbox popover ships box-shadow 0 12px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.18) (styles.css:220) — 4x the blur, ~3x the alpha. Digest entries carry no shadows at all.

criteria.finding: One overlay shadow exceeds the bound; entry-level elevation is absent everywhere else. Scored 2 rather than lower because the excess sits on a floating overlay container, not on entries.

scoreBasis: Ladder: the subject sits at the highest anchor it fully satisfies. c1 (one foreign inline hue) and c2 (accent decorating every entry) hold the subject at anchor 1 — either alone would. c3 and c4 record what the surface must add or shed to climb; they cannot lift a subject still carrying a foreign inline hue.
notScored: Semantic state colors on trust surfaces — danger on failed items, warning on suggested pills, green on accepted/ready, accent tint on needs_review blocks. The trust-surfaces contract governs those and this rule explicitly may not override it.

Whether the chrome grays are hue-linked to the terracotta accent (obs-mew-tokens/f3) — answering requires resolving every CSS custom property to computed values, which code reading alone cannot do reliably. Not assessed.
The command palette and room chrome outside the two note surfaces.
Runtime rendering — no computed-style audit was performed for this baseline.
boundary: Scored from source at commit 9c99889f. Hex literals were read directly from the stylesheets; CSS variable fallbacks were taken at face value. A computed-style audit could move c4 if the popover shadow is overridden at runtime, and could open the obs-mew-tokens/f3 gray-tinting question this receipt declined to score.
